scope: Existing borrowed HF technical and target-runtime evidence only; original facts, source-level review dates and conflicts are unchanged.

sections: Key points for upgrading to version 10.0
Support for version 3.7 of the Python runtime environment has been removed
claims.qualification: Heavy Forwarder uses the Enterprise package. October 22 bounded semantic recheck: Python 3.9 is the 10.0 default, Python 3.7 support is removed, and apps and add-ons must be compatible with 3.9. This does not establish UF applicability, compatibility for every installed or app-owned runtime, or a deployment approval.

sections: Key points for upgrading to version 10.0 — FIPS-mode module requirements and dedicated migration link
claims.qualification: Heavy Forwarder uses the Enterprise package. The 10.0 source introduces a FIPS 140-3-compliant module for FIPS-mode instances. The linked procedure separates the version upgrade from FIPS module migration and verifies forwarding before migrating the indexing tier. Scope is the FIPS-mode Enterprise package. UF applicability and regulated authorization remain separate.

supportingSources.section: Phase 2: How to Migrate Splunk Enterprise from FIPS 140-2 mode to FIPS 140-3 mode; Procedure for Migrating Splunk Enterprise from FIPS 140-2 mode to FIPS 140-3 mode > Migrate the forwarding tier from FIPS 140-2 to FIPS 140-3

sections: Key points for upgrading to version 10.0 — SSL 3.0 and TLS 1.0/1.1 deprecation
claims.qualification: Heavy Forwarder uses the Enterprise package. October 21 bounded semantic recheck: SSL 3.0 and TLS 1.0/1.1 remain supported in 10.0 with warnings while deprecated; the source recommends TLS 1.2 or higher and anticipates certificate work. This is not 10.4 removal, a UF requirement or a deployment approval.

sections: Key points for upgrading to version 10.2 — Python runtime defaults and opt-in
The Splunk platform uses version 3.13 of the Python runtime environment on Splunk Web
The Splunk daemon and its associated components can now use version 3.13 of the Python interpreter, version 3.9 is still available
claims.qualification: Heavy Forwarder uses the Enterprise package. This mapping verifies the cited section for the existing record, not UF applicability, every installed app, or a deployment approval. October 18 bounded semantic recheck: Splunk Web 3.13 is distinct from splunkd 3.9 default and optional 3.13 in the 10.2 source; later 10.4 default changes remain separate. The November 11 review also checked the exact 10.2 upgrade summary against the separate Web and splunkd sections.

sections: The Node.js JavaScript runtime environment has been removed
claims.qualification: November 6 semantic recheck: the Enterprise 10.2 section removes bundled Node.js and requires Node.js-dependent apps to carry their own runtime. Heavy Forwarder inherits only the applicable Enterprise-package scope. Visual Exporter is assessed independently in SVD-2026-1015. No UF runtime, Cloud-managed installation requirement or app-owned vulnerability conclusion is inferred.

sections: Splunk Enterprise no longer lets you run it as the root user by default
claims.qualification: Heavy Forwarder uses the Enterprise package. October 22 bounded semantic recheck: Splunk Enterprise 10.2 blocks root execution by default on Unix-like systems, permits the temporary --run-as-root override, and recommends a least-privileged non-root account. This does not establish UF applicability, every installed app's identity requirements, or deployment approval.

sections: The Splunk Fishbucket database back end has been replaced
claims.qualification: Heavy Forwarder uses the Enterprise package. October 22 bounded semantic recheck: the replacement backend reads legacy checkpoints and writes new checkpoints without an explicit or implicit migration. An unsupported downgrade can miss newer checkpoints and cause reingestion or duplicate data. This does not establish UF applicability, checkpoint loss during a supported upgrade, or a supported rollback path.

supportingSources.section: The Splunk Fishbucket database back end has been replaced — legacy checkpoint reads, new writes and unsupported downgrade behavior

sections: Upgrade Splunk Python version from 3.9 to 3.13
claims.qualification: Heavy Forwarder uses the Enterprise package. October 22 bounded semantic recheck: Enterprise 10.4 uses Python 3.13 by default and keeps Python 3.9 as a fallback for applications that are not yet compatible. This does not establish UF applicability, compatibility for every installed or app-owned runtime, or deployment approval.

sections: Splunk has removed support for versions 1.0 and 1.1 of the Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol

supportingSources.section: Turn on support for older TLS versions with deprecatedTlsVersionSupport

claims.qualification: Heavy Forwarder uses the Enterprise package. The 10.4 READ THIS FIRST says TLS 1.0/1.1 support was completely removed, while the versioned 10.4 TLS guide says both are off by default and describes a temporary, restart-required opt-in with known security risks. Use TLS 1.2 or higher for inter-Splunk connections. The 10.6 removal of the opt-in is a separate release fact. The conflict does not establish UF applicability, a Cloud-managed requirement, or deployment approval.

sections: Splunk removed support for Secure Hash Algorithm 1 (SHA1) certificate signatures
claims.qualification: 10.0 deprecation precedes 10.4 removal; reissue certificates at SHA-256 or stronger. Enterprise-package customer-managed HF scope.

sections: Splunk removed older unsupported MongoDB database engine binaries
claims.qualification: 10.4 READ THIS FIRST limits the change to the Enterprise package across OSes and instructs KV Store users to reach MongoDB 7 or higher first. The current exact heading replaces the older heading. Component-dependent HF scope; no UF or Cloud-managed host inference.

sections: Upgrading the backend database for KV Store and KV Service to MongoDB 8.0
claims.qualification: Heavy Forwarder uses the Enterprise package. October 26 bounded semantic recheck: the 10.4 release page says older MongoDB 4.x-6.x binaries are absent, 9.x-and-earlier deployments must bridge through Enterprise 10.0 or 10.2, and an already-10.x deployment upgrades the database automatically. This verifies the cited component scope, not UF applicability, every installed app, rollback safety or deployment approval.

sections: Splunk changed how App Key Value Store (KV Store) uses TLS-related settings in the [kvstore] stanza of the server.conf configuration file
claims.qualification: Heavy Forwarder uses the Enterprise package. October 20 bounded semantic recheck: overlapping KV Store TLS settings previously ignored in favor of sslConfig now take precedence in kvstore. Review both stanzas and unused/conflicting settings. This does not reverse the precedence, apply to UF, or certify all HF components.

sections: Splunk Enterprise on Windows no longer lets you install, upgrade, or run it as an administrator-level user
claims.qualification: Windows-only branches differ for local-system, domain-administrator and local-service accounts. Non-administrator domain accounts remain possible.

sections: Prepare for upgrade
Optional: Postpone the automatic database upgrade to a cohosted KV store before it begins
claims.qualification: Applies only to an Enterprise-package HF with KV Store. October 25 bounded semantic recheck: the current guide requires KV Store 7.0+, more than 50% free disk space, health checks and a parallel backup; migration starts automatically unless postponed, impairs writes, and requires ITSI 5.0.x and lower to postpone with postgresMigrateOnStartup=false verified on every member. ES incompatibility remains separately cited to the matrix; omission here is not clearance. No UF applicability, pairing, entitlement or authorization is inferred.

sections: Splunk has removed support for versions 1.0 and 1.1 of the Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol
claims.qualification: Heavy Forwarder uses the customer-managed Enterprise package. The 10.6 upgrade notice says the temporary TLS 1.0/1.1 option was removed. The separate 10.6 configuration guide still documents the opt-in. Retain the published conflict and validate TLS 1.2 or 1.3 before upgrading. Do not rely on the legacy setting or infer UF, Cloud-managed or app-owned runtime applicability.

claims.qualification: October 25 bounded semantic recheck: the KV Store guide requires 10.2 or higher before 10.6 for sources at 10.0 or lower and KV Store 7.0+ before the 10.6 transition; the general Enterprise 10.6 table still lists a direct 10.0 route. Preserve both exact scopes without editing the general graph or applying this KV-specific prerequisite to UF.
